title: What does ISO/IEC 27001:2022 require for awareness and training?
description: How ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clauses 7.2 and 7.3 and Annex A control 6.3 shape information security competence, awareness and training, and what auditors check.
shortAnswer: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires an organization to determine the competence needed by people whose work affects information security, ensure they are competent, act to close gaps and keep evidence (clause 7.2), and make sure people are aware of the security policy, their contribution and the implications of not conforming (clause 7.3). Annex A control 6.3 adds an ongoing awareness, education and training program for personnel and relevant interested parties.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2 (competence) is a mandatory requirement for certification: determine, ensure, act and evaluate, and retain documented evidence.
Clause 7.3 (awareness) covers the information security policy, each person's contribution to the ISMS, and the implications of not conforming.
Annex A 6.3 is a people control on awareness, education and training; it is applied through the risk assessment and Statement of Applicability.
The 2024 amendment (ISO/IEC 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024) added climate action changes and did not alter the competence and awareness clauses.
Auditors look for evidence of competence and effectiveness, not just course completions.
regulator: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), through accredited certification bodies
appliesTo: Organisations certified or seeking certification to ISO/IEC 27001
Suppliers required by customers or government to hold ISO/IEC 27001
Organisations using ISO/IEC 27001 as a governance reference without certification

sections.heading: Which version of ISO/IEC 27001 is current?

blocks.text: As at September 2026, the current edition is [ISO/IEC 27001:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/27001), Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection: Information security management systems: Requirements, together with [Amendment 1:2024](https://www.iso.org/standard/88435.html), titled Climate action changes. The amendment concerns climate considerations and leaves the competence and awareness requirements unchanged.

ISO/IEC 27001 is voluntary. It becomes binding through certification, customer contracts or procurement rules. In regulated sectors it often sits alongside statutory or government security obligations, and one training program can serve several frameworks if its mapping is explicit. **Example, Australia:** regulated entities and agencies may also need to meet [APRA CPS 234](/regulations/apra-cps-234-security-awareness-training) or the [ISM](/regulations/ism-cyber-security-awareness-training).

sections.heading: What does clause 7.2 require for competence?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2 requires the organization to define and prove competence for everyone doing work under its control that affects information security performance. In summary, the organization must:

items: determine the necessary competence of those persons
ensure they are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience
where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence and evaluate the effectiveness of those actions
retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence

blocks.text: The standard notes that actions can include training, mentoring or reassigning current staff, or hiring or contracting competent people. Training is therefore one route to competence, not the requirement itself. A person with the right experience and evidence may need no course; a person who completed a course but cannot perform the task is not yet competent. That distinction is the core of [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification).

sections.heading: What does clause 7.3 require for awareness?

blocks.text: Clause 7.3 requires everyone doing work under the organization's control to be aware of three things: the information security policy; their contribution to the effectiveness of the information security management system (ISMS), including the benefits of improved performance; and the implications of not conforming with ISMS requirements.

Awareness applies to a broader group than competence. Clause 7.2 targets people whose work affects security performance, while clause 7.3 covers all persons doing work under the organization's control, which in practice includes contractors and temporary staff.

sections.heading: What does Annex A control 6.3 add?

blocks.text: Annex A 6.3, information security awareness, education and training, is a people control that calls for personnel and relevant interested parties to receive appropriate awareness, education and training, plus regular updates of the organization's policies and procedures relevant to their job. Implementation guidance sits in [ISO/IEC 27002:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/75652.html).

Unlike clauses 7.2 and 7.3, Annex A controls are selected through risk treatment and justified in the Statement of Applicability. In practice almost every ISMS includes 6.3, because excluding it is difficult to justify. It replaced control A.7.2.2 from the 2013 edition, with the same basic purpose.

blocks.text: Auditors test whether competence is defined, achieved, evaluated and evidenced, and whether awareness is real when they interview staff. Completion certificates on their own rarely satisfy clause 7.2 because they do not show the competence was defined or that training was effective.

sections.heading: Where do organizations commonly fall short?

blocks.text: The most common gap is treating a single annual awareness course as the answer to clause 7.2, 7.3 and Annex A 6.3 together. The course may satisfy 7.3, but it does not define role competence or evaluate effectiveness.

items: No written competence requirements for ISMS roles, so there is nothing to assess against.
No evaluation of effectiveness, which clause 7.2 requires where actions are taken.
Contractors and third parties left out of awareness, despite clause 7.3 covering all persons doing work under the organization's control.
Training content not updated after policy changes, which undermines Annex A 6.3.
Evidence scattered across systems, making it hard to produce during a surveillance audit.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines ISMS role competencies and awareness concepts as structured objects with assessment points, then links them to clauses 7.2 and 7.3 and to Annex A 6.3. The same concepts can be mapped to the regulatory obligations of each jurisdiction, so one body of evidence answers several frameworks.

faqs.q: Does ISO/IEC 27001 say how often awareness training must happen?
faqs.a: No. The standard does not set a frequency. Annex A 6.3 expects regular updates as policies and procedures change, and organizations set their own cycle, commonly annual awareness with extra briefings after significant changes. Where a regulator or government security framework sets an annual requirement, that usually sets the cycle.

faqs.q: Are training records enough to meet clause 7.2?
faqs.a: Usually not. Clause 7.2 requires the organization to determine the necessary competence, ensure people are competent, evaluate the effectiveness of actions taken and retain evidence of competence. A completion record shows attendance, not that the defined competence was achieved.

faqs.q: Did the 2024 amendment change training requirements?
faqs.a: No. ISO/IEC 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024 is titled Climate action changes and concerns climate considerations. The competence, awareness and Annex A 6.3 provisions are unchanged, so training programs built for the 2022 edition remain aligned.

faqs.q: Do suppliers and contractors need ISO 27001 awareness training?
faqs.a: Clause 7.3 covers all persons doing work under the organization's control, which includes contractors working within the ISMS scope. Annex A 6.3 also refers to relevant interested parties. Organizations either train them directly or require equivalent training through contract terms and check the evidence.
